output_list.reason: The mintToken function has an integer overflow vulnerability. The totalSupply and balances[owner] variables are incremented without a check, allowing the owner to set the balance of any user to any value, and subsequently to any total supply, due to a lack of overflow protection in the addition operation.

The transfer function has an integer overflow vulnerability. The _value parameter is not checked for overflow in the subtraction operation balances[msg.sender] -= _value, allowing users to set balances to a negative value, and subsequently to any total supply, due to a lack of overflow protection in the subtraction operation.

The transferFrom function has an integer overflow vulnerability. The _value parameter is not checked for overflow in the following operations: balances[_to] += _value, balances[_from] -= _value, and allowed[_from][msg.sender] -= _value, allowing users to set balances to a negative value, and subsequently to any total supply, due to a lack of overflow protection in the subtraction operations.

The approve function has a wrong logic vulnerability. It allows the owner to set the allowance of any user to any value, without preventing a re-entrancy attack where a spender can repeatedly request funds from an account compromised by this vulnerability.
The disableToken function has an access control vulnerability. It allows the owner to disable the token transfer function, but the owner can also enable it, due to a wrong logic in the function.
